entities.name: Diclofenac
observations: Rectal diclofenac is used as prophylaxis to reduce post-ERCP pancreatitis; retrieved evidence did not establish benefit for intramuscular administration.

entities.name: Post-ERCP pancreatitis
observations: Pancreatitis occurring after endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography; rectal NSAID prophylaxis reduces incidence.

entities.name: Rectal NSAID effect
observations: Meta-analysis of 25 NSAID trials involving 7,688 patients found post-ERCP pancreatitis reduced with NSAIDs (pooled OR 0.598, 95% CI 0.47–0.76); rectal diclofenac/indomethacin reduced PEP.

entities.name: PMID:37981523
observations: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 25 randomized trials (7,688 patients); NSAIDs reduced PEP, with pooled prevalence 0.598 (95% CI 0.47–0.76); rectal diclofenac and indomethacin reduced PEP.

entities.name: PMID:37160838
observations: A real-world cohort using prophylactic rectal diclofenac plus selective pancreatic-duct stenting had PEP odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.31–0.93) versus historical controls; NNT 22.

entities.name: PMID:39215866
observations: Retrospective comparison found PEP in 8.2% of patients receiving rectal diclofenac (25/304) and 8.2% receiving rectal indomethacin (60/728); it compared active treatments, not placebo.
